And then Petrovic answered, He's in Belgrade visiting his family. There were some other officers present there, I can't exactly remember, I think Lieutenant-Colonel Kerkez and some others. I can't remember their names, but I remember this particular event for certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of this Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Rajko Petrovic. He worked as a an employee in the financial station.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could you give us the name of the lieutenant-colonel that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Zeljko Kerkez.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you link, or, rather, do you link this particular event to a particular date? I'm sorry. You've already told us that. You've mentioned the 11th of July. Can you explain what do you link that date with, why has it stuck in your memory?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I remember it because later on, in the evening, just before darkness fell, I don't remember the exactly time, we were informed that in view of the fact that Rajko Petrovic had a three-digit number on the automatic exchange that I mentioned, that the army of Republika Srpska had entered the town of Srebrenica; and that is why I remember that date so well. Because we were having the this roast that day, so I remember it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Pajic, I ask you a technical question linked to your profession. From which locations within the territory of Republika Srpska was it possible to send an encoded telegram with the heading of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: It was possible to send it from any command post of a brigade or a corps, wherever there was an encryption, teleprinter station it could be sent. Wherever there was an encryption, teleprinter station, a telegram could be sent regardless of the header.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And if it is sent from the brigade, is it directly addressed to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No, not to the Main Staff, but to the superior unit. If it's going from the brigade, then it is sent to the corps. In the corps, the encoders reprocess the telegram and dispatch it to the Main Staff. And then from the Main Staff, it is sent to units and institutions to which it is addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would end my examination-in-chief there, and I wish to thank the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Zivanovic, you had asked for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will have a few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day Mr. Pajic. My name is Dragan Krgovic, on behalf of General Gvero's Defence, I will put a few questions to you that have to do with your testimony today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 6D178.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pajic, you have a telegram -- a recipient telegram, that's how I would put it, an incoming telegram. I don't think you've seen this document before, but it fulfills the conditions you referred to when answering questions from my colleague, Mr. Petrusic. When he asked you whether a document was drafted in accordance with the regulations; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in the block signature, you can see the name of Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic, which shows that he signed this incoming telegram. My question is as follows: Does this necessarily mean that Mr. Pandurevic actually signed the document, or is it possible that someone signed this telegram on his behalf?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Well, he could have signed this document but not necessarily. If someone signed for him, usually you have “for” pencilled in, but an encryption teleprinter cannot convey this information, this element. So he could have signed it and someone else may have signed it. So the telegram should have been signed by the person who drafted the telegram or by someone representing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Or by someone who had the right to send such a telegram?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The person who is authorised by the commander to act in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just clarify this again. He could have signed it but not necessarily. Sometimes someone would pencil in "for" and then you would have a signature. But an encryption teleprinter cannot transmit this handwritten signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown Exhibit 6D177. 177, 177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document is under seal, so there will be no broadcast of it, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pajic, this is, in fact, the outgoing telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is what you were referring to, in fact, the person who signed the telegram isn't Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic. Someone signed on his behalf, and in the incoming telegram this signature and the signature of the other person are not visible, do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Well, let's me tell you, this is an act, not a telegram. This wasn't processed by an encryption teleprinter. You just have a stamp that shows that it was received through the encryption teleprinter after it was typed out on a certain device --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: This witness is kindly asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- this is an act that was issued by the encryption teleprinter, and it was drafted in order to be sent out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please slow down. It's difficult for the interpreters to follow you.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will just give a hard copy of this document so that you can compare the contents and see whether we're dealing with the same contents. Usher, could you please be of assistance? In the first case, the document was supposed to be outgoing, and this is an incoming telegram; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: The document without a handwritten signature was received by the Drina Corps command, and this is a coded act from the Zvornik Brigade. It was supposed to be sent out as a telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The contents are identical practically speaking?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I wasn't really looking at the contents. I was trying to see whether the form was regular, and the form of the documents are quite regular.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, this is a document that was encoded, and the other document was received by the Drina Corps. I am talking about the transmission of the first document. The second document is a transmission of the first one?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pajic, I now draw the conclusion that if you have an incoming telegram and you have a signature on the telegram, it doesn't mean that the individual concerned actually signed the document sent. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I'll repeat this. With regard to the incoming telegram, the document that was encrypted, the encrypted telegram can't show a handwritten signature, so the person can sign it or someone can sign on behalf of someone else. Here we can see that someone signed on behalf of someone else. There was the encryption teleprinter in Zvornik that was supposed to forward a telegram.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You have just confirmed what I said; you said "yes" in response to my answer. But the question -- or, rather, your answer "yes" wasn't recorded in the transcript. Could you repeat that you, in fact, agreed with my claim?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat what you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When an incoming telegram arrives in a unit, and you can see the signature or, rather, a block signature of a certain individual, that does not mean that that individual actually signed the document in question. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with what you have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will move on to another subject now. So if it's a good time to have a break, I have another ten minutes -- oh, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but the break is in almost 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a little confused in the afternoon sittings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you want, we can cancel sitting in the afternoon; after all, they're all afternoons sittings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you would be doing me a big favour, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pajic, as far as I have noticed when responding from my colleague, Mr. Petrusic, you said you were born in Rogatica; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was born in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And I assume that before you went to be schooled outside of Rogatica, you lived in Rogatica; and your family lives in that area ; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you're familiar with the area around Rogatica and Zepa; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I know it quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pajic, did your family live in the sector between Rogatica and Zepa in the summer of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. My parents lived in the village called Babljak, which is in the Borike local commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name of the village?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Babljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it's in the immediate vicinity of the first combat lines dividing the army of Republika Srpska and the Zepa Brigade in the Zepa secretary. It's not far from there; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the summer of 1995, did you have the opportunity of visiting your parents and relatives; in fact, did you go home?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but not that often, occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pajic, can you tell me is there -- between Rogatica and Zepa were there any checkpoints of the army of Republika Srpska? I'm not referring to the checkpoint at the entrance to Rogatica on the upper side.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: In 1995, I think there was a checkpoint at the cross roads towards Visegrad and Borike at a place called Lijesce --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreter heard the name correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- there was a checkpoint there occasionally. I can't give you a precise date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And towards Zepa, were there any checkpoints towards Zepa going from Rogatica towards Zepa, were there any checkpoints there?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Well only at Boksanica, there was one there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: At the very entrance to the enclave?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No, at Boksanica. Up there, UNPROFOR was up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had UNPROFOR in mind, but I don't remember the army of Republika Srpska having any checkpoints and apart from that, there was this checkpoint at Lijesce.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pajic, tell me, how far is Rogatica to Zepa by car? How much time do you need to get there by bus or in a convoy? According to information I had at the time, well, it took between an hour and an hour and a half; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, given that a large section of the road from Mrkonic to Zepa was a macadam road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Pajic, I have no more questions for you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye, we still have ten minutes to go. You can start, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Unless you prefer to delay it until after the break, it's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I think now is a good time to start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon to you, and Your Honours, good afternoon to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And good afternoon to you, Mr. Pajic. My name is Kweku Vanderpuye, and on behalf of the Prosecution, I am going to put some questions to you in relation to your direct examination and also in relation, perhaps, to your cross-examination. If there is anything that I ask you that's unclear to you, please let me know and I will try to restate it or rephrase it in a way that we can best understand one another. Now, I think I want to work backwards in relation to your testimony, but you wound up, your direct testimony, talking about information that you received concerning Mr. General Miletic's whereabouts on the 11th of July 1995. Do you recall giving that testimony?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, on the 11th of July, you were on duty; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was at G1 the morning of the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And G1 is located where, at Crna Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you recall specifically on that day you were at a party, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And where was the party exactly?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: At a distance of 7 to 8 kilometres from G1 at Crna Rijeka. This was a cottage settlement called Hans Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what time did you go to this party?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact time. It could have been at some point between 9.00 and 10.00 that morning. I drove over in order to set up the barbecue for everyone else who was coming. I went there with Mr. Rajko Petrovic, who was the organiser.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And on that day when you went to the party, who was on duty in the communications unit?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly who was on duty. Apart from me, there were other workers there who were in charge of establishing and maintaining communications, telegram communications, telegraph communications. I believe the man duty that day was Domazet Sekula, who was an employee of the army of Republika Srpska, but I cannot be positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Apart from Mr. Sekula, who else would have been on duty that day in the communications unit?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: There were a number of other people who might have been on duty such as Zarko Tanasic, Nenad Ristic, Blagode Abazovic, Marijan Jerot, Slobodan Mandic, that's about it, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I take it that some of these gentlemen, if not all of them, went to the party as well?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember any of them being there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: By the way, what day of the week was this; if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: It was Tuesday I think, but I'm not positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you recall this day in particular because you received some information that the army had gone into Srebrenica on that day, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What other information did you receive that day concerning the army?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Nothing special, not on that day. We had this barbecue at the party. We were simply not really in touch with G1, aside from the fact that someone got in touch with Mr. Petrovic on the phone telling him that the army of Republika Srpska had entered Srebrenica. There was really nothing special aside from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you don't know anything, or you didn't learn at that time anything about a bombing, a NATO bombing, of VRS positions?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. Nothing special really. I wasn't really following closely, there were operations that were underway all along the front line; and I wasn't showing a special interest. It's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You say you weren't following closely? I just want to make sure that I've got that right.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I wasn't really following too much whatever was going on. I was just doing my job and that was that. I wasn't really following on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, your job had to do with conveying messages and orders, et cetera, essentially from the Main Staff to subordinate units, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat that? I didn't hear the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your job had to do with conveying messages, orders, from the Main Staff through the radio lines, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No. My job was to establish and maintain those communications, and that alone. Other people were in charge of the actual transmission of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you had no idea what information was being conveyed from the Main Staff down to the subordinate units throughout your period of time in service; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: That's right. That wasn't my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So as you've testified here rather extensively about the form and the nature and the process of sending telegrams, that's based on something you learned about but not something you actually did as a job during the war, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: As I've pointed out already, I actually completed an encryption course for teleprinters. I didn't actually do that encrypt or dispatch telegrams, but in principle I knew how this was done and how a telegram like that was properly received; but that wasn't what I was doing at the time. I was in charge of maintaining radio relay links, keeping them up and running at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So when you were asked a question about whether or not the rules were followed at the Main Staff in relation to the form that telegrams, et cetera, were sent, that's not based on some evaluation that you did of those documents, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: There are rules in the work of an encryption post, how a telegram is dispatched, and that had to be followed. Whenever one did not follow the rules, you couldn't call the resulting document a telegram.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Time for the break, 25 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Pajic. The last question I asked you answered had to do with whether or not the rules -- or what your knowledge was concerning the rule as it applied to the transmissions of telegrams, orders, et cetera, from the Main Staff to its subordinate units. And what I asked you was -- or what I want to know, I should say, is you don't have any actual knowledge as to how those documents acts, orders, as it were, were actually transmitted, whether or not they were done -- that was done in accordance with the rules or not in accordance with the rules, because, A, you didn't inspect those transmissions or those documents; and B, that wasn't you line of work during your service; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. That wasn't my line of work. Nevertheless, I did attend meetings where certain things were agreed, such as the way documents were sent, and there was the instruction that one should comply with the rules. The encryption officer would see to that, they said. As far as the morning reports were concerned, ones that I looked at, I don't remember any problems in terms of the compliance with the rules in as far as the documents were concerned that were being sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. Now, you recall hearing from Rajko Petrovic that Mr. -- I should say General Miletic was in Belgrade, that was on 11th July, 1995, right? You have that specific recollection today, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You have a specific recollection today that that was a Tuesday, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I think it was a Tuesday, but I can't be positive. I do think so, though. I probably didn't check at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You have no recollection today as you're testifying that on that day, the 11th of July, that certain positions were bombed, and in particular, your commander, Mladic, was involved in such a bombing?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You have no recollection today about the circumstances that were faced by Chief of Staff Milovanovic on the western front on that day?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No, none. I know that he wasn't at the Main Staff at the time, General Milovanovic; but I don't remember what was going on along the western front at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you have no recollection today, as you testify, about the circumstances occurring in Trnovo around that time, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, being on duty, you went, you said, to set up this barbecue in morning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And from whom did you obtain permission to go set up this barbecue?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I obtained permission from the company commander for the garrison and communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And who is the company commander for the communications unit that you were in?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: At the time, or, rather, as the company commander was not around, the person standing in for him was Warrant Officer Dragan Nedimovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what did you tell your company commander or the person standing in for him, Mr. Nedimovic, what did you tell him in relation to your leaving of your post?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Nedimovic, Mr. Nedimovic, warrant officer who was standing in for the company commander -- garrison and communications company commander. I told him that I had been invited by Rajko Petrovic to help him organise the barbecue and that I would be on the way to give him a hand, and he okayed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when were you invited, by the way, to this barbecue by Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: In principle we had agreed several days, but he called me the night before we were supposed to organise this barbecue, and we agreed on a time and place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how many people attended this barbecue?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: As I said, I don't remember exactly how many people were there, but I reckon between 15 and 20 people; but I can't be positive. Probably about 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when did it occur?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: 11th of July, 1995. I got there between 10.00 a.m. and 11.00 a.m. along with Rajko. We set the whom thing up, we grilled the meat, we set up the tables and benches, and then at about 2.00 or 3.00 p.m., the others got there as well once the whole thing had been sets up.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did this occur at his house or at some other location?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: It was next to a house that he was renting at the time, where he was living with his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, today is not the first day that you've spoken about this party and the information that you heard from Mr. Petrovic regarding General Miletic's whereabouts, is it?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I take it you've spoken to the Defence about this particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When was the first time that you mentioned to the Defence of General Miletic the circumstances surrounding this party as you've indicated here today?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd of October, this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And have you discussed it with them since?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When did that occur?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: The 3rd of October, that afternoon, at Rogatica. I spoke to Counsel Petrusic, I discussed this with him. The reason being, quite simply, eventually I ended up asking myself why are they accusing this man if, for example, I remember the 11th, the 11th being etched in my mind because of what happened with the army of Republika Srpska and during Srebrenica. I know that he was not at the Main Staff that day. I don't know when he went away or when he returned, but I know he wasn't there on the day. And I can state that with certainty, he was not at the Main Staff that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Maybe there was an error in the translation, but I asked you if you had spoken to the Defence since the 3rd of October; that is, between the 3rd of October and today, and is your answer "yes"?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I talked to them about it on the 3rd and when I got here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in relation to your discussions with the Defence, did you come to learn of another party that occurred at some other time in relation to the whereabouts of Mr. -- or General Miletic?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the other party. I certainly wasn't there, so I never discussed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You never discussed with the Defence anything about General Miletic's whereabouts other than on the 11th of July, 1995, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: That's right. We had met on the 23rd of August that same year. I think Counsel Petrusic drew a diagram or rather we drew a diagram together of the underground facility, and I knew at the time that General Miletic was in the detention unit already.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the 23rd of August? Because that's what's recorded in the record here.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: On or about the 23rd, I think so. I'm afraid I can't be more specific, but the 23rd of August, and he was in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And would that be the first time that you met with the defence concerning General Miletic or was there yet another occasion?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: A total of three meetings. There was another one before that one which occurred sometime in January or February that same year. I can't remember the date for our first meeting or the time, but we met a total of three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say, "January and February of that same year," you mean this year, 2008? So --

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So I would be correct then in saying that you met with them in January or February of 2008, and then again in August of 2008, and then again in October of 2008, and then again now, or recently, of November 2008; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I can't be specific about the first meeting. I know that it was winter time. It might have been December the previous year, I know it was winter time, was it December, the previous year, January or February this year; now that's something I can't confirm for you. As for the other meetings that took place I told you already what the timeline would be for those.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. So from your testimony I gather you did not mention to them anything about General Miletic being away for the command when you met with them in January or February and when you met with them again in August?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: That's right. I mentioned nothing until the 3rd of October. The previous meetings were mostly about communications documents and how the communications system was organised. Eventually, I asked what all of this was about, because I knew for a fact that the man was not there on that day date, on the 11th, he wasn't at the Main Staff. So eventually I raised the question on the 3rd of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How did it become a matter of importance to you where he was on the 11th of July suddenly in October of 2008?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: It didn't suddenly become important, I simply remembered the period, and I asked myself why, in view of the duties he had, and the fact that I knew that he wasn't there on that day, I simply remembered that date. I don't know how to explain this to you, but it was a date that stuck in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you drew a diagram, you said? When you drew the diagram representing how things we are laid out, was that anchored to any particular period of time such as July of 1995 or the summer of 1995? I think it was 5D1395.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I made the diagram in August after the second meeting, and it's a sketch of the underground part of the facility, the way it was; and that was how the premises were laid out throughout. Sometimes the communication devices would and the staff would move from the above-ground facility to the underground facility, but this diagram applied to the underground part of the G1 facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that the witness and the Prosecutor are talking about the same sketch, and I would like to give this diagram to the witness so as to remove any misunderstandings. It is the same diagram that was shown today, only in a different format.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. Thank you, Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have no objection to it. I haven't seen that particular diagram, but I would like to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, will you make it available then, Mr. Petrusic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Usher, please. Have him put it on the ELMO, please. All right. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is the diagram that you say that you drew in August of this year?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the diagram, but I forgot to indicate a room between the operations centre and here where the chief of departments were. I didn't draw it on that occasion. I just left out this one room when I drew it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well --

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: So there is one additional room to those drawn here, which I had forgotten at the time because of a certain accident I had, and I forgot all these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, your recollection, I take it, then, on 19th November was better than it was back in August when you drew this, right? 19th of November, just so you know, was the date that's written on the document that's in evidence, it's 5D1395. Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you've got me at a bit of a disadvantage here because unfortunately I can't read what's written here, but the point is when you drew this diagram, that is the one that's on the ELMO now, in August of 2008, was this intended to reflect the way these rooms were laid out in July of 1995? In other words, was that brought to your attention at that time?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is how it was in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that was what this was intended to reflect, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you met with the Defence in January or February of 2008, it was also brought to your attention that the events that they were concerned about, with respect to communications or radio relay devices, had to do with July of 1995. They made that clear to you, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You know somebody by the name of Vojislav Babic?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I do know Vojislav Babic. In 1995, he was chief of staff of the 67th Communications Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you ever discuss Vojislav Babic in any respect with the Defence before your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No, no I didn't discuss Vojislav Babic. I just knew that he was due to come here to testify, but nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you ever tell the Defence that in relation to Mr. Babic -- did you ever tell the Defence or explain to the Defence that the barbecue that you attended had nothing to do with Mr. Babic's birthday which related to a party or an event that occurred on 7 July 1995? Did you ever tell them about that or did they ever discuss that with you?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't discuss that with me at all, and I am not aware of that party yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. All right. Mr. Pajic, I just want to acquaint you with something that I received from the Defence, and it talks about this party on the 7th. And in part, and I will offer that later on. It says: "Mr. Babic spoke about his birthday party and the Witness Pajic explained today, 16 November, that the barbecue had nothing to do with Mr. Babic's birthday. So it seems that these were two separate occasions, one on the 7th and one on the 11th." Did you explain to the Defence that the barbecue that you went to had nothing to do with Mr. Babic's birthday, did you have that discussion at all?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't discuss that. I just know that Babic did not attend this barbecue on the 11th of July 1995. I don't know when Babic's birthday is, and I was not aware of that party.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And just so that I am clear, you never had that discussion at all in any of your meetings with the Defence; that is, either in January or February or August or October or November of 2008?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that, sir. Now, you testified some about the organisation of the communications network, if you will, as regards the Main Staff. And in order for the Main Staff to communicate with subordinate units, you said that this could transpire over a secure line; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say "subordinate units" you mean corps and brigades and battalions and so forth, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: The Main Staff had organised communications only with the corps. The units attached to staffs, the army of Yugoslavia, the presidency, the government, and the Assembly of Republika Srpska, those were the main lines of communication; whereas, the corps organised communications with their subordinate unit, brigades, and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of the organisation of the communications of the corps, the Main Staff would be apprised of that, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That way if you needed to reach somebody within a brigade you knew how to do it from the Main Staff, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the way you would communicate in -- from the Main Staff to the corps would be through a wire line from Crna Rijeka to Veliki Zep and over a radio, radio relay, from Veliki Zep to whatever subordinate unit you try and reach, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was how it was except for the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps where we had alternatives between relay and wire lines. Though we combined the communications because it was not possible to organise radio relay connection with this corps, part of the route was covered by wire connections.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In terms of the security of the communications, for example, from the Main Staff to the Drina Corps, that is for voice communications, those were protected in so far as their transmission from the Main Staff to Veliki Zep; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: That is correct. There were two relay directions between Veliki Zep and the Drina Corps. One was protected and the other one was unprotected.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall specifically what those lines were?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I do. The protected line was 0674, that is, the number it had in 1992; and in 1993 it was 0658. And the other is 07 -- sorry 0607, that was the analogous line. 0674 was protected up to a certain point of time, and then it was 0658, and the analogous one was 0607. In this one FM200 was operational because it is the only one that can be operational under a regime of protection; whereas, for the other it was not possible to protect it, to secure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just so we know, the FM200 is a device that's similar to an RRU800, right? It operates within the same range -- same frequency range, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Well, they are not similar, but they do use the same frequency range.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, if I could I'd like to show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- 65 ter 2893. Sorry, my fault, 2823.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I am showing you is the -- essentially what is a frequency plan. It's a Drina Corps document. It's dated 2 October 1993, and it sets out radio relay routes. If you look at item number 2 at the bottom of -- well, it's in the middle of the page in your language, and it's the bottom of page 1 in the English. It sets out command of the Drina Corps, this is the radio relay direction versus -- towards Veliki Zep, do you see that? It says radio relay Bravac RRPR, number 0607, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the radio relay route, 0607, that I mentioned just a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And there is another radio relay route 0674 that you indicated, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, 0604, I said that the number was subsequently changed, and it became 0658 around 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: 0658 changed -- it was changed in 1993? Is that right or did it change to that in 1993?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: In 1993, it was changed into 0658.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So this document, October 2nd, 1993, doesn't reflect the correct relay route numbers as they existed in 1993, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Well, that was probably changed towards the end of the year. I know that it was in 1993 that we would usually change the route number. So only the route number was changed, but the links themselves were not affected. Everything remained the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What about the frequencies, did they change, or did they stay the same, too?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No, the frequencies weren't changed. They remained the same. We only changed the route number for the document, but as far as the frequencies are concerned, everything remained the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Have you seen this document before by the way?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: You're asking whether I've seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: I'm -- never had the opportunity of seeing it before because it's a telegram from the Drina Corps, and they only informed us about the frequencies of their devices since the chief of communications of the Main Staff gave his authorisation for the frequencies and for changes frequencies. I'm familiar with this document when it came to the Main Staff because the chief of communications of all the corps asked for an overview of the frequencies at radio relay stations, of the situation at radio relay stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Who sets the frequencies that are on these radio relay paths?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: At the hubs, at all the hubs of the Republika Srpska army, the frequency plan was adopted by the chief of the communications of the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska army, and at the radio relay hubs that belong to the army of Republika Srpska, Tvren [phoen], Strazbenice, well, it was the chief of communications of the army of Yugoslav Army who authorised these frequencies. We couldn't the change the frequencies at Strazbenice and at Cer without the authorisation of the chief of communications of the army of Yugoslavia, naturally of the request of the chief of communications of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska. So the communications at the hubs of the army was Republika Srpska were authorised by the chief in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the chief in the Main Staff would be somebody by the name of Prole, chief of communications?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: The chief of communications of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska was Colonel Radomir Prole.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Prole, PR; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Prole, P-R-O-L-E.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And when you talk about the ability to change the frequencies, what about the hubs that were in the territory of the RS, what about those?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Well, as I said, those frequencies could only be changed at the order of the chief of communications of the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska army. There was some kind of an annual plan; however, there were divergencies. So as of 1993 up until 1995, well, I don't remember having ever changed those frequencies during that time-period, because the hubs that we mostly used at Strazbenice and Cer, well the frequency plan had to be authorised by the chief of communications of the communications 18 administration of the army of Yugoslavia; so we didn't change the frequencies that often. It wasn't done annually. I know that in 1992, 1993, these frequencies weren't changed and that was the case until the end of war. If necessary, if there were any disturbances one would go one or two megahertz up or down, during the disturbance, and then go back to the same one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So as far as you're aware, the frequencies that were used to communicate, for example, from the Main Staff through to, say, Zvornik, those frequencies never changed throughout the war in your experience, right?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I take it you're shocked to hear that communications along those lines were intercepted? Is that news to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have any information about that. In a way, yes, but it's technically possible to intercept such communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were in charge of maintaining the communication lines, radio relay lines, and you're telling us here today that you have no information throughout the entire war that those lines were being intercepted by your enemy? Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: VELO PAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't have any concrete information. I didn't have any documents showing that such and such a route at such and such a time was intercepted. I didn't have such information; although, I received unofficial information according to which certain communication routes were being intercepted. This had to do with the RRU1 exclusively, the RRU1 device exclusively. I knew about that so I insisted on using a device for cryptographic protection. I am talking about the RRU1 device, which could be intercepted or, rather, it was more easy to intercept this device than it was to intercept other devices that used higher frequencies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it might be a good time to break with your permission, otherwise I could certainly fill it up until 7.00 on the dot, if you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. President. Could I have 2821, please, in e-court. And if we could go to the next page. It's under subheading number 5. I think it's page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is taking too long. Let's leave it. Let's leave it. We'll continue tomorrow as the same time as today, 2.15 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: 6.59 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 26th day of November, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.
